agreement_type.name: Educational Affiliation Agreement for Student Internships
agreement_type.description: Clinical/practicum placement agreement between Exos and a Institution or Institution.

entries.label: Parties & Recitals
entries.description: Who is bound; the Institution/Company/Student framing.

entries.label: Renewal / Auto-Renewal
entries.description: Whether and how the agreement renews.

entries.label: Termination for Convenience
entries.description: Non-renewal / no-fault exit and notice period.

entries.label: Termination for Cause
entries.description: Breach, cure period, immediate termination triggers.

entries.label: Indemnification
entries.description: Who bears third-party claim risk; mutual vs one-way.

entries.label: Insurance
entries.description: Required coverage types and limits; student health insurance.

entries.label: FERPA / Student Records
entries.description: Handling of education records under FERPA.

entries.label: Background Checks
entries.description: Right to screen students before placement.

entries.label: Amendments
entries.description: How the agreement may be modified.

entries.label: Accreditation & Licensure
entries.description: Both parties' duty to maintain qualifications.

entries.label: Limitation of Liability
entries.description: Liability caps and exclusions (often absent; flag if introduced).

entries.label: Non-Compete
entries.description: Superseded by Non-Exclusive; flag if a true non-compete appears.

entries.label: IP Ownership Assignment
entries.description: Rare here; activate if IP terms appear.

entries.label: Minimum Commitment
entries.description: Placement counts are discretionary, not committed.

entries.label: Audit Rights
entries.description: Inspection right exists but not a financial audit; revisit.

observed_positions.full_text: Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure.   The Institution agrees to maintain confidentiality and shall not disclose any 'Confidential Information' of the Facility. ' Confidential Information '  means  any  and  all  information  disclosed  by  the  Facility,  including,  without limitation, to financial information, customer lists, agreements, marketing information, business plans, trade secrets or other intellectual property, and including any protected health information (' PHI ')  as  defined  within  HIPAA, disclosed  in  any  manner  and  regardless  of  whether  such information is specifically labeled as such. Confidential Information shall not include information that is required to be disclosed by the Institution pursuant to judicial order or other compulsion of law, provided that the Institution shall provide to Facility prompt notice of such order and comply with any protective order imposed on such disclosure. Students will sign and comply with the Facility's  Confidentiality  and  Non-Disclosure  Agreement,  attached  hereto  as  Exhibit  A  and incorporated herewith.

observed_positions.full_text: 7.1 Definition. ' Confidential Information ' means all information obtained by the receiving party related to or provided  by  the  disclosing  party  or  its  affiliates,  and  all  information  derived  therefrom,  but  excludes information that: (a) is or becomes available to the general public other than through a breach of duty to the disclosing party; (b) was lawfully in the receiving party's possession prior to receipt under this Agreement; (b) is  independently developed by the receiving party without reference to Confidential Information; or (c) is subsequently  obtained  from  a  third  party  without  restriction  or  breach  of  an  obligation  to  the  disclosing party. observed_positions.text_summary: 7.2 Obligations. Receiving party will protect Confidential Information of the disclosing party with reasonable care and  will  not  disclose  it  to  any  third  party,  or  use  it  for  any  purpose
observed_positions.full_text: 7.2 Obligations. Receiving party will protect Confidential Information of the disclosing party with reasonable care and  will  not  disclose  it  to  any  third  party,  or  use  it  for  any  purpose,  except  as  permitted  under  this Agreement. Receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to persons who need to know it who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than in this Section 7. Receiving party will be liable for any breach of this Section 7 by any person obtaining Confidential Information from it.  The foregoing notwithstanding, receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent  necessary to comply with any law or governmental order if it first notifies disclosing party and provides it with an opportunity to prevent or limit such disclosure. To the  extent permitted by law, receiving party will  destroy Confidential Information of the disclosing party upon request, other than backup copies not readily accessible.

observed_positions.text_summary: 10.1. Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure. Notwithstanding the protections for HIPAA-protected information set forth above, Exos is responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of any other propriet
observed_positions.full_text: 10.1. Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure. Notwithstanding the protections for HIPAA-protected information set forth above, Exos is responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of any other proprietary or confidential information and will limit its disclosure of such information to those who need to know it. Exos will not disclose trade secrets to students or to Institution. The Institution will require students, to the extent that students gain access to proprietary information designated by the Exos as confidential, to comply with policies and practices of the Exos designed to protect the confidentiality of this information. Nothing in this agreement shall be deemed to prevent any individual from complying with applicable law or court order. Exos understands that Institution is subject to the Virginia Freedom of Information Act, which may require disclosure of records within the possession of the School. Institution will inform its Students of EXOS’ requirement to sign and comply with Exos's Confidentiality Agreement, attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herewith.

Clinical Training Confidentiality Agreement
This Confidentiality Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made by and between the Counterparty-64 \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ (School and Department) on behalf of Counterparty-34 (“Counterparty-64”) whose principal place of business is \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\, and [Company] whose principal place of business is \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ (“Discloser”).
Counterparty-64 provides academic programs and training related to clinical services.  As part of [specific Counterparty-64 clinical program], Counterparty-64 assigns students to affiliated clinical facilities to complete clinical training consistent with the educational objectives of the academic program.  Discloser desires to collaborate with Counterparty-64 in the development and implementation of such clinical training during the course of which Discloser may disclose to Counterparty-64 and its students (hereinafter referred to as “Recipients”) certain data, specifications, samples, materials, research information, new product development initiatives, business plans, and business objectives, which are competitively sensitive, proprietary, and/or confidential to Discloser (the “Confidential Information”).  Discloser will not disclose to Recipients in connection with the clinical training any information that it considers a trade secret.
In consideration of the mutual promises exchanged herein and other good and valuable consideration, the Discloser and Counterparty-64 agrees as follows:
Recipient agrees to accept in strict confidence and not use for its own benefit or divulge to a third party Discloser’s Confidential Information designated as proprietary and confidential, either on its face or in a separate writing provided by Discloser to Recipient within ten (10) days of any disclosure, except in furtherance of the clinical training and then only to persons who have agreed to maintain the information as confidential.
The confidentiality obligations outlined in this Agreement shall not be binding on Recipient with respect to any Information which:
(a) is rightfully in the possession of Recipient at the time of disclosure; or
(b) is or becomes known to the public generally through no fault or other action of Recipient; or
(c) is obtained lawfully by Recipient on a non-confidential basis from a third party; or
(d) is developed by Recipient as a result of its own efforts, without the use of, or access to, the Confidential Information received from Discloser; or
(e) is required by law or legal order to be disclosed by Recipient.
Recipient will destroy all written, including electronic Confidential Information received from Discloser or which incorporates or references any Confidential Information of Discloser (including all copies thereof) at the request of Discloser.
Unless otherwise agreed in writing signed by both parties, Recipient agrees not to disclose any Confidential Information of Discloser for a period of three (3) years after disclosure of such Confidential Information.
For the avoidance of doubt, the clinical training includes discussion between Counterparty-64 students and Counterparty-64 faculty as part of the students’ academic course of study, and no exchange of information in the context of this academic course of study will be deemed a breach of this Agreement.
This Agreement contains the entire understanding hereto relative to the Confidential Information.  This Agreement may not be amended or supplemented except in a written agreement signed by both parties.  The terms and conditions contained in this Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia.
Recipient recognizes and agrees that nothing in this agreement shall be construed as granting any rights to Recipient, by license or otherwise, to any Information of Discloser, except as specified in this Agreement.
In order to indicate acceptance of this above-mentioned terms and conditions, the parties have signed this letter in the space herein provided by an officer duly authorized.

Assigning Students to the Exos’ facilities. After receiving the number of placements available for Students from Exos, the Institution shall submit information about the Students selected to be considered (with the approval of Exos) for the Program.  Following review, Exos may approve the Students to be placed at one of Exos’ facilities. The Institution shall notify the Students assigned to the Exos facility, and Exos of each Student’s availability for participation in clinical experiences. Exos may place Students at one of its Affiliate’s facilities. Upon any such placement,, this Agreement will be deemed to be made exclusively between the Institution and Exos’ Affiliate identified on the Student’s internship paperwork (offer letter, confidentiality agreement, or the like) and the other Exos Affiliate signatories hereto shall be automatically withdrawn as a party.  The term “Affiliate” means an entity as of or after the Effective Date owned by, controlling, controlled by, or under common control with, directly or indirectly, a party, whether through ownership of voting securities or other equity interest, representation on its board of directors or other governing body, or by contract.

Educational Affiliation Agreement for Student Internships
Institution (“Institution”)	Address & Email
(Institution Name)
The Institution offers educational programs (“ Programs ”) for students (“ Students ”) in physical therapy, exercise science, and/or related health fields at various locations (each, a “ Facility ”). Programs include unpaid, supervised clinical experiences at a Facility. Exos will collaborate with the Institution to provide Programs aligning with the Institution's educational objectives.

observed_positions.full_text:
RECITALS
The Institution administers educational curricula for students pursuing careers in physical therapy, exercise science or other related health professions (each referenced herein as " Student ," collectively, “ Students ”), and seeks to provide, as part of the educational curricula, supervised clinical experiences for Students at the Facility (the “ Program ”);
The Facility seeks to provide Students of the Institution with supervised experiences at the Facility sites, consistent with the educational objectives of the Institution; and
The Facility and the Institution have determined that each may best accomplish its objectives by mutual assistance and seek to describe their affiliation in this Agreement.
In consideration of the mutual promises and conditions in this Agreement, the Facility and the Institution agree as follows:
AGREEMENT
INSTITUTION’S RESPONSIBILITIES .  In addition to its responsibilities described elsewhere in this Agreement, the Institution shall have the following responsibilities:
Preparation of Students for Facility Placement .  The Institution shall assure, through qualified faculty, that each Student assigned to the Facility is adequately prepared to benefit from such assignment.  Student's preparedness shall be measured by: (i) academic performance indicating an ability to understand what Student will observe and/or perform during the clinical placement; and (ii) appreciation of the nature and seriousness of the work Student will observe and/or perform.

DESCRIPTION  OF  CONFIDENTIAL  INFORMATION .  Any  and  all  information disclosed  by  Facility, including  but  not  limited  to financial  information,  customer  lists, agreements, marketing information, business plans, trade secrets or other intellectual property, and including any protected health information as defined within the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), disclosed in any manner and regardless of whether such information is specifically labeled as such, is considered confidential information, unless such information falls within the exceptions set forth below (hereinafter such information shall be collectively referred to as 'Confidential Information').

observed_positions.full_text: RELATIONSHIP OF PARTIES. Nothing in this Agreement is intended or shall be construed to create a joint venture relationship,  employment  relationship,  a  partnership,  a  lease,  or  a  landlord/tenant  relationship. observed_positions.text_summary: Initial and Renewal Term. Subject to Section 6.2 below, this Agreement shall be effective as of the date set forth above (" Effective Date ") and shall continue for an initial term of five (5) years.
observed_positions.full_text: Initial and Renewal Term. Subject to Section 6.2 below, this Agreement shall be effective as of the date set forth above (" Effective Date ") and shall continue for an initial term of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew and continue in full force and effect for any and all periods during which any Student in the Program is placed at the Facility. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may choose not to renew this Agreement at the end of the then-current Program by providing the other with not less than sixty (60) days' advance written notice of its intent not to renew prior to the end of then-current Program. In the event that either party's non-renewal of this Agreement disrupts the clinical experience of any Student(s) in the Program, the Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until such time as this Agreement may expire without disruption of said Student(s)' clinical experience. Upon notice of non-renewal by either party, no new Student may be placed at the Facility.

Thereafter,  this Agreement shall automatically renew and continue in full force and effect for any and all periods during which any Student in the Program is placed at Exos. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may choose not to renew this Agreement at the end of the then-current Program by providing the other with not less than sixty (60) days' advance written notice of its intent not to renew prior to the end of then-current Program. In the event that either party's non-renewal of this Agreement disrupts the clinical experience of any Student(s) in the Program, the Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until such time as this Agreement may expire without disruption of said Student(s)' clinical experience. Upon notice of non-renewal by either party, no new Student may be placed at any Exos facility.

our_standard.text:
Overview
Institution Responsibilities | Exos Responsibilities | Joint Responsibilities
- Provide information reasonably requested about Students to enable Exos to evaluate their candidacy. - Ensure Students are prepared for the Program by qualified faculty, with measured academic performance. - Coordinator to manage Students’ educational experiences for the Program. - Maintain accreditations/ licenses required of an educational institution. | - Determine which Students may participate in the Program and assign them to a Facility. - Offer Students clinical experiences meeting accreditation standards. - Appoint “Facility Coordinator” to oversee clinical experience and enable Student activities based on the agreed objectives. - Orient Students to the Program and applicable Exos rules and policies. - Maintain qualifications/ licenses required to provide clinical experiences to Students. - Promptly notify Institution of any student injuries, and arrange medical care per its policies, but without financial responsibility. | - Meet periodically to review key Program objectives. - Cooperate to supervise and evaluate Students, including providing feedback on Student’s performance throughout the Program.

INSTITUTION'S  RESPONSIBILITIES.  In  addition  to  its  responsibilities  described elsewhere in this Agreement, the Institution shall have the following responsibilities:
Preparation of Students for Facility Placement. The Institution shall assure, through qualified faculty, that each Student assigned to the Facility is adequately prepared to benefit from such  assignment.  Student's  preparedness  shall  be  measured  by:  (i)  academic  performance indicating an ability to understand what Student will observe and/or perform during the clinical placement; and (ii) appreciation of the nature and seriousness of the work Student will observe and/or perform.

Overview
The Institution offers educational programs (' Programs ') for students (' Students ') in physical therapy, exercise science, and/or related health fields at various locations (each, a ' Faci
observed_positions.full_text:
Overview
The Institution offers educational programs (' Programs ') for students (' Students ') in physical therapy, exercise science, and/or related health fields at various locations (each, a ' Facility '). Programs include unpaid, supervised clinical experiences at a Facility. Exos will collaborate with the Institution to provide Programs aligning with the Institution's educational objectives. Facilities locations are specified at: [url redacted]/location/contact.
Institution Responsibilities | Exos Responsibilities | Joint Responsibilities
● Subject to FERPA, provide information reasonably requested about Students to enable Exos to evaluate their candidacy. ● Ensure Students are prepared for the Program by qualified faculty, with measured academic performance. ● Coordinator to manage Students' educational experiences for the Program. ● Maintain accreditations/ licenses required of an educational institution. | ● Determine which Students may participate in the Program and assign them to a Facility. ● Offer Students clinical experiences meeting accreditation standards. ● Appoint 'Facility Coordinator' to oversee clinical experience and enable Student activities based on the agreed objectives. ● Orient Students to the Program and applicable Exos rules and policies. ● Maintain qualifications/ licenses required to provide clinical experiences to Students. ● Promptly notify Institution of any student injuries, and arrange medical care per its policies, but without financial responsibility. | ● Meet periodically to review key Program objectives. ● Cooperate to supervise and evaluate Students, including providing feedback on Student's performance throughout the Program.

observed_positions.full_text:
Overview
The Institution offers educational programs (' Programs ') for students (' Students ') in physical therapy, exercise science, and/or related health fields at various locations (each, a ' Facility '). Programs include unpaid, supervised clinical experiences at a Facility. Exos will collaborate with the Institution to provide Programs aligning with the Institution's educational objectives.
Institution Responsibilities | Exos Responsibilities | Joint Responsibilities
● Provide information reasonably requested about Students to enable Exos to evaluate their candidacy. ● Ensure Students are prepared for the Program by qualified faculty, with measured academic performance. ● Coordinator to manage Students' educational experiences for the Program. ● Maintain accreditations/ licenses required of an educational institution. | ● Determine which Students may participate in the Program and assign them to a Facility. ● Offer Students clinical experiences meeting accreditation standards. ● Appoint 'Facility Coordinator' to oversee clinical experience and enable Student activities based on the agreed objectives. ● Orient Students to the Program and applicable Exos rules and policies. ● Maintain qualifications/ licenses required to provide clinical experiences to Students. ● Promptly notify Institution of any student injuries, and arrange medical care per its policies, but without financial responsibility. | ● Meet periodically to review key Program objectives. ● Cooperate to supervise and evaluate Students, including providing feedback on Student's performance throughout the Program.

A. AGENCY Responsibilities
To provide students in the Institution access to all AGENCY facilities as is appropriate for the fulfillment of suitable internship experiences (job-like or practical experie
observed_positions.full_text:
A. AGENCY Responsibilities
To provide students in the Institution access to all AGENCY facilities as is appropriate for the fulfillment of suitable internship experiences (job-like or practical experiences) during the period of the Internship Program. The AGENCY has the overall authority of the facilities and grounds and for the safety of persons therein.
The beginning and ending date for the Internship Program shall be set by the Institution. However, the individual days and hours the intern shall attend within that period shall be arranged as agreed upon between the AGENCY and the student.
The AGENCY shall be able to submit to the Institution a description of its current plan for the Internship Program, including objectives, learning activities, responsibilities of the students, nature of supervision provided, and such other information as may be necessary to outline the content of the Internship Program. The AGENCY shall also provide information to the Institution regarding facilities, housing, transportation, medical examination, testing and immunization requirements, other special requirements or restrictions, and other such information as may be useful for the students to know in advance.
To maintain appropriate accreditation status by appropriate accrediting agencies.
To provide instructional supervision appropriate for the student's level of preparation and continued learning. The internship experience should be structured such as to meet the mutually accepted objectives of internship experience agreed upon by the Institution and the AGENCY. However, it is understood that students shall not be used in lieu of professional or staff personnel and shall be under appropriate AGENCY supervision at all times.
To provide, in writing, to the Institution (if asked) the name and professional and academic credentials of the person responsible for supervising the Internship Program at the AGENCY (hereinafter referred to as the Agency Supervisor).
To provide the student with orientation to the AGENCY, including its rules, regulations, and any applicable safety programs and the location and usage of any machinery and any personal protective equipment necessary. Also, the student may be asked to sign a statement of nondisclosure agreement on confidentiality, professional appearance, and professional behavior, if so required by the AGENCY.
The AGENCY agrees to inform the Institution of any changes in staffing or in its service program that will affect the Internship Program of the student. The AGENCY will make every effort to inform the Institution of such changes at least one month in advance of commencement of the Internship Program.
To provide first aid and emergency medical care for illnesses or accidents occurring on the premises. All medical and dental costs are the responsibility of the student.
To retain responsibility for the care of its clients.
To be responsible for and retain absolute control over the organization, administration, operation and financing of its services.
The AGENCY agrees to inform both the Institution and the student concerning the student's level of internship growth and competence and to complete as least two evaluation reports on forms to be provided by the Institution. The evaluation process shall include a conference between the student and Agency Supervisor at the times of completion of reports. The evaluation reports shall be sent to the Institution internship representative (hereinafter referred to as the Internship Coordinator). The AGENCY further agrees to maintain such other records as may be requested by the Institution to evaluate each student's performance in the Internship Program.
The AGENCY agrees, upon reasonable request made by the Institution, at any time during or after the Internship Program, to permit inspection of its facilities, student records, or other records or items which pertain in any way to the Program of the Institution's students, by the Institution and accrediting agencies. However, this does not include access to patient records, protected by privacy rules under Federal HIPPA statutes. The AGENCY agrees not to dispose of or destroy such records for a period of 6 months after the termination of the AGREEMENT.
To reserve the right to withdraw or dismiss any student whose clinical performance is unsatisfactory, or his/her behavior is disruptive or detrimental to the AGENCY and/or their client(s). The AGENCY shall inform the Institution of any such withdrawal or dismissal in a timely fashion, preferably within one business day, if possible.
The AGENCY may conduct background checks on any student prior to or during the Internship Program, in compliance with applicable federal and state laws.

16. Institution Responsibilities
The Institution will designate a faculty member to be the Internship Coordinator. The Internship Coordinator will serve as the liaison between the AGENCY and the UNIVERS
observed_positions.full_text:
16. Institution Responsibilities
The Institution will designate a faculty member to be the Internship Coordinator. The Internship Coordinator will serve as the liaison between the AGENCY and the Institution. In the event that it becomes necessary to cancel reserved space or change a student's assignment, the Institution will make every effort to notify the AGENCY in advance of the scheduled beginning of the Internship Program period.
To coordinate through proper AGENCY channels the planning for the appropriate Internship Program.
The Institution shall be responsible for selecting only those students who have successfully completed the prerequisite course to complete the Internship Program. The STUDENT shall be responsible for completing any other prerequisites required by the AGENCY.
The Institution shall inform the AGENCY of the level of training the students have received prior to placement with the AGENCY. The Institution shall provide the AGENCY with current information about its curriculum and internship education goals.
The Institution may withdraw any student from the Internship Program whose progress, achievement or adjustment does not appear to justify his/her continuing with the Internship Program. Wherever possible, such withdrawal shall be planned cooperatively by the Institution and the AGENCY.
Furthermore, it is expressly agreed and understood that the students participating in the Internship Program shall not be deemed employees, agents, or servants of the AGENCY for any purpose, nor shall they be entitled to any fringe benefits, workers' compensation, disability, unemployment or any other benefits or rights normally afforded to employees of the AGENCY.
The Internship Coordinator shall provide the AGENCY with student roster, internship objectives, and internship schedule prior to the beginning of the Internship Program.
To assign students to the Internship Program only when mutually arranged by the Institution and the AGENCY.
To maintain channels of communication for exchange of information with the
AGENCY by on-site visits when practical and by telephone in other instances.
The Institution shall notify the student that he or she is responsible for:
a. Adhering to ethical and professional practices of maintaining confidentiality of the AGENCY's client and corporate information. The student must sign a confidentiality statement prior to beginning the Internship Program, if the AGENCY so requires.
b. Adhering to the administrative policies, standards, and practices of the AGENCY.
c. Attending all pertinent activities involving the AGENCY to which he/she is assigned.
d. Providing appropriate uniform or any necessary individual equipment where required.
e. Any personal property.
f. All transportation and living arrangements.
g. Providing documentation of student's medical clearance prior to the beginning of the student Internship Program, if so required by the AGENCY. Medical clearance may include but is not limited to status of hepatitis B vaccination or signed refusal; tetanus, T.B. screening, proof of rubella and rubeola vaccination or antibiotics; proof of negative PPD no older than 6 months prior to internship experience (if positive, must show negative chest x-ray).
h. Providing the AGENCY evidence of health insurance, if so required by the AGENCY.
i. Obtaining prior written approval from the AGENCY and the Institution before publishing any material relating to the Internship Program.
j. Providing the AGENCY proof of appropriate Professional Liability Insurance during the term of the Internship Program, if so required by the AGENCY.
k. GENERAL PROVISIONS
The Institution will disclose information from a student's educational record, as appropriate to personnel at the AGENCY who have a legitimate need to know in accordance with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act. The AGENCY hereby agrees that its personnel will use such information only in furtherance of the Internship Program for the student, and that the information will not be disclosed to any other person without the student's prior written consent.
The AGREEMENT may be modified by written amendment signed by a duly authorized representative of each party.

The Institution offers educational programs (' Programs ') for students (' Students ') in physical therapy, exercise science, and/or related health fields at various locations (each, a ' Facility '). observed_positions.full_text:
C.	Institution RESPONSIBILITIES
The Institution shall make the material provided by the AGENCY describing the Internship Program at the AGENCY available to students at the Institution.
The Institution shall provide faculty and/or staff to serve as resource personnel and program consultants to assist the AGENCY staff in appraising, analyzing and evaluating programs, teaching techniques, methods, and processes concerned with the Internship Program.
The Institution shall develop a means of evaluation of the AGENCY and its Internship Program for TRAINEES and share the results of each evaluation with the AGENCY.
The Institution shall provide forms to be completed by the AGENCY supervisor for evaluation of TRAINEES.
The Institution advisor or designated representative shall visit the AGENCY (if within a 90-mile radius from the Institution), during each training period in which a TRAINEE is assigned to the AGENCY.  The visitation shall include conferences with the AGENCY’s director of the Internship Program, AGENCY supervisors, and TRAINEES.
The Institution shall inform AGENCY in writing of approval as an Internship Program site.
The Institution shall consider input into the curriculum from the AGENCY.
The Institution shall provide, in accordance with the confidentiality of information regulations, any additional information about any TRAINEE which would have an effect on the TRAINEE’S ability to successfully complete the Internship Program.

observed_positions.full_text:
D.	AGENCY RESPONSIBILITIES
The AGENCY shall provide students of the Institution opportunity for placement equivalent to those of other schools having an affiliation agreement with the AGENCY provided the students meet the requirements for placement.
The AGENCY shall permit inspection of its educational facilities, student records and any other items which may be needed to meet accreditation requirements of the Institution'S program.
The AGENCY shall provide a written description of the Internship Program being offered to students in its entirety and shall give a plan to the Institution (faculty sponsor) and to each TRAINEE assigned to the AGENCY.
The AGENCY shall furnish a supervisor to work with the Institution in administering and coordinating the Internship Program.
The AGENCY, through its supervisor, is responsible for the assignment of TRAINEES to acceptable activities staffed by capable and qualified personnel.
The AGENCY shall provide a full-time staff member qualified in education, registration and experience to directly supervise the TRAINEE and will submit a written description of the staff member's qualifications.
The AGENCY shall complete and submit the evaluation forms supplied by the 			Institution.
The AGENCY shall submit a list of cooperating personnel, with such required information as needed, for the Institution to extend status and privileges as allowed by Institution policy.
The AGENCY will agree to carry appropriate comprehensive general liability and professional liability insurance for its officers, agents, and employees, and the AGENCY, that said insurance coverage would in existence during the term of this Agreement, and proof thereof submitted to the Institution.

The Institution offers educational programs (' Programs ') for students (' Students ') in physical therapy, exercise science, and/or related health fields at various locations (each, a ' Facility '). Programs include unpaid, supervised clinical experiences at a Facility. Exos will collaborate with the Institution to provide Programs aligning with the Institution's educational objectives.
Institution Responsibilities | Exos Responsibilities | Joint Responsibilities
● Provide information reasonably requested about Students to enable Exos to evaluate their candidacy. ● Ensure Students are prepared for the Program by qualified faculty, with measured academic performance. ● Coordinator to manage Students' educational experiences for the Program. ● Maintain accreditations/ licenses required of an educational institution. | ● Determine which Students may participate in the Program and assign them to a Facility. ● Offer Students clinical experiences meeting accreditation standards. ● Appoint 'Facility Coordinator' to oversee clinical experience and enable Student activities based on the agreed objectives. ● Orient Students to the Program and applicable Exos rules and policies. ● Maintain qualifications/ licenses required to provide clinical experiences to Students. ● Promptly notify Institution of any student injuries, and arrange medical care per its policies, but without financial responsibility. | ● Meet periodically to review key Program objectives. ● Cooperate to supervise and evaluate Students, including providing feedback on Student's performance throughout the Program.
The parties are aware that there are constitutional and statutory limitations on the authority of Counterparty-24 (a state agency) to enter into certain terms and conditions of the Agreement, including, but not limited to, and limitations of warranties; disclaimers and limitations of liability for damages; waivers, disclaimers and limitations of legal rights, remedies, requirements and processes (including waiver of jury trials); limitations of periods to bring legal action; granting control of litigation or settlement to another party; liability for acts or omissions of third parties; payment of attorneys' fees; mandatory dispute resolution; indemnities; and confidentiality (collectively, the 'Limitations'), and any terms and conditions incorporated herein to the extent rendered unlawful by the Limitations, will not be binding on the Counterparty-24 .
This agreement is between Exos, [address redacted], [address redacted], [email redacted] (' Exos '), and the ' Institution ' named above, and it is governed by the Educational Affiliation Terms for Student Internships at [url redacted]/hubfs/Legal/education-affiliates.pdf (the ' Terms '). This agreement and Terms (together, the ' Agreement ') are the entire understanding of Exos and Client relating to Programs. No other service agreement, purchase order, online or other terms apply.

observed_positions.full_text: 3.1 Supervision and Evaluation of Students. The Institution and Exos shall, in good faith, work cooperatively to assure adequate supervision and evaluation of Students while Students are on-site at Exos. Both parties shall reinforce with Students: (i) the seriousness of the service being performed at Exos, including Student's impact upon the well-being of Exos's clients; (ii) the importance of abiding by Exos's rules and regulations; and (iii) the confidentiality of Exos client's identities and personal information. The Institution shall, if Exos so desires, assure prompt feedback to Exos regarding Students' evaluation of the clinical experience at Exos. Exos shall provide feedback to the Institution regarding Students' performance at Exos' facility.

observed_positions.full_text: 1.1 Preparation of Students for Exos Placement. The Institution shall assure, through qualified faculty, that each Student  assigned  to  an  Exos  facility,  as  mutually  agreed,  is  adequately  prepared  to  benefit  from  such assignment.  Student's preparedness shall be measured by: (i) academic performance indicating an ability to understand what Student will observe and/or perform during the clinical placement; and (ii) appreciation of the nature and seriousness of the work Student will observe and/or perform.

observed_positions.full_text: 1.4 Assigning Students to the Exos' facilities. After receiving the number of placements available for Students from Exos, the Institution shall submit information about the Students selected to be considered (with the approval of Exos) for the Program.  Following review, Exos may approve the Students to be placed at one of Exos' facilities. The Institution shall notify the Students assigned to the Exos facility, and Exos of each Student's availability for participation in clinical experiences. Exos may place Students at one of its Affiliate's facilities. Upon any such placement,, this Agreement will be deemed to be made exclusively between the Institution and Exos' Affiliate identified on the Student's internship paperwork (offer letter, confidentiality agreement, or the like) and the other Exos Affiliate signatories hereto shall be automatically withdrawn as a party.  The term ' Affiliate ' means an entity as of or after the Effective Date owned by, controlling, controlled by, or under common control with, directly or indirectly, a party, whether through ownership of voting securities or other equity interest, representation on its board of directors or other governing body, or by contract.

The Institution and Exos shall, in good faith, work cooperatively to assure adequate supervision and evaluation of Students while Students are on -site at Exos. Both parties shall reinforce with Students: (i) the seriousness of the service being performed at Exos, including Student's impact upon the well -being of Exos's clients; (ii) the importance of abiding by Exos's rules and regulations; and (iii) the confidentiality of Exos client's identities and personal information. The Institution shall, if Exos so desires, assure prompt feedback to Exos regarding Students' evaluation of the clinical experience at Exos. Exos shall provide feedback to the Institution regarding Students' performance at Exos' facility.

observed_positions.full_text: 1.1 Preparation of Students for Exos Placement. observed_positions.full_text: 1.4 Assigning Students to the Exos' facilities. After receiving the number of placements available for Students from Exos, the Institution shall submit information about the Students selected to be considered (with the approval of Exos) for the Program. Following review, Exos may approve the Students to be placed at one of Exos' facilities. The Institution shall notify the Students assigned to the Exos facility, and Exos of each Student's availability for participation in clinical experiences. Following review, Exos may approve the Students to be placed at one of Exos’ facilities. The Institution shall notify the Students assigned to the Exos facility, and Exos of each Student’s availability for participation in clinical experiences. Exos may place Students at one of its Affiliate’s facilities. Upon any such placement, this Agreement will be deemed to be made exclusively between the Institution and Exos’ Affiliate identified on the Student’s internship paperwork (offer letter, confidentiality agreement, or the like) and the other Exos Affiliate signatories hereto shall be automatically withdrawn as a party.  The term “ Affiliate ” means an entity as of or after the Effective Date owned by, controlling, controlled by, or under common control with, directly or indirectly, a party, whether through ownership of voting securities or other equity interest, representation on its board of directors or other governing body, or by contract.

observed_positions.full_text: 3.1 Supervision and Evaluation of Students. The Institution and Exos shall, in good faith, work cooperatively to assure adequate supervision and evaluation of Students while Students are on-site at Exos. Both parties shall reinforce with Students: (i) the seriousness of the service being performed at Exos, including Student's impact upon the well-being of Exos's clients; (ii) the importance of abiding by Exos's rules and regulations; and (iii) the confidentiality of Exos client's identities and personal information. The Institution shall, if Exos so desires, assure prompt feedback to Exos regarding Students' evaluation of the clinical experience at Exos. Exos shall provide feedback to the Institution regarding Students' performance at Exos' facility.

Student's preparedness shall be measured by: (i) academic performance indicating an ability to understand what Student will observe and/or perform during the clinical placement; and (ii) appreciation of the nature and seriousness of the trainingStudent will observe and/or perform.

rejected.full_text: 1.4. Assigning Students to the Exos’ facilities. After receiving the number of placements available for Students from Exos, the Institution shall submit information about the Students selected to be considered (with the approval of Exos) for the Program.  Following review, Exos may approve the Students to be placed at one of Exos’ facilities. The Institution shall notify the Students assigned to the Exos facility, and Exos of each Student’s availability for participation in clinical experiences. Exos may place Students at one of its Affiliate’s facilities.

rejected.full_text: 1.4. Assigning Students to the Exos’ facilities. After receiving the number of placements available for Students from Exos, the Institution shall submit information about the selected Students approved by Exos for the Program. Exos may place Students at one or more of Exos’ facilities. After the Institution notifies Students assigned to the Exos facility, the Institution will inform Exos of each Student’s availability for participation in the Program. Upon notice at any time by access to Institution, the Agreement, as it pertains to a given Student, will be deemed assigned to an Exos Affiliate on behalf of which intern is providing services to Exos’ clients. The term “Affiliate” means an entity as of or after the Effective Date owned by, controlling, controlled by, or under common control with, directly or indirectly, a party, whether through ownership of voting securities or other equity interest, representation on its board of directors or other governing body, or by contract.

rejected.full_text: 2.4. Orientation. Failure to do so shall be grounds for Students’ immediate removal from participation in the Program.

our_standard.text: 1.8. Term. Unless otherwise specified in an agreement referencing these Terms, this Agreement is effective as of the Effective Date for an initial term of five years. Thereafter, it will automatically renew for successive one-year periods, unless either party provides at least 60 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal, to be effective as of the end of the then-current term; provided, however, that non-renewal shall not disrupt the clinical experience of any Student actively serving in the Program, and the Agreement shall remain effective as to such Student(s) until the end of their clinical experience. Following non-renewal by either party, no new Students will be placed at any Facility.

For Cause. In the event the Institution or the Facility fails in any substantial manner to perform as required herein, this Agreement may be terminated as described below:
Either  party  may  terminate  this  Agreement  at  any  time,  upon material breach of any of its provisions by the other party; provided, however, that not less than thirty (30) days prior to termination, written notice shall be given by the non-breaching party to the breaching party that states the intention of the non-breaching party to terminate this Agreement,
the nature of the material breach giving rise to termination and shall permit the breaching party reasonable opportunity to cure such material breach during said thirty (30) day period (" Cure Period ").
If the material breach is not resolved to the satisfaction of the nonbreaching party during the Cure Period as provided in Section 6.2 (B)(1) above, the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the breaching party.
In  the  event  that  termination  of  the  Agreement  by  the  Facility pursuant to this Section 6.2 (B) disrupts the clinical experience of any Student(s) in the Program, the parties shall attempt, in good faith and using their best efforts, to continue Students' clinical experiences,  and  this  Agreement  shall  remain  in  full  force  and  effect  until  such  time  as  this Agreement may expire without disruption of said Students' clinical experience. During any time period in which notice of termination has been given and existing Students are completing the Program, no new Student may be placed at the Facility.

For Cause. In the event the Institution or the Facility fails in any substantial manner to perform as required herein, this Agreement may be terminated as described below:
Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time, upon material breach of any of its provisions by the other party; provided, however, that not less than thirty (30) days prior to termination, written notice shall be given by the non-breaching party to the breaching party that states the intention of the non-breaching party to terminate this Agreement, the nature of the material breach giving rise to termination and shall permit the breaching party reasonable opportunity to cure such material breach during said thirty (30) day period ("Cure Period").
If the material breach is not resolved to the satisfaction of the non-breaching party during the Cure Period as provided in Section 6.2 (B)(1) above, the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the breaching party.
In the event that termination of the Agreement by the Facility pursuant to this Section 6.2 (B) disrupts the clinical experience of any Student(s) in the Program, the parties shall attempt, in good faith and using their best efforts, to continue Students’ clinical experiences, and this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until such time as this Agreement may expire without disruption of said Students’ clinical experience. During any time period in which notice of termination has been given and existing Students are completing the Program, no new Student may be placed at the Facility.

our_standard.text:
Overview
Institution Responsibilities | Exos Responsibilities | Joint Responsibilities
- Provide information reasonably requested about Students to enable Exos to evaluate their candidacy. - Ensure Students are prepared for the Program by qualified faculty, with measured academic performance. - Coordinator to manage Students’ educational experiences for the Program. - Maintain accreditations/ licenses required of an educational institution. | - Determine which Students may participate in the Program and assign them to a Facility. - Offer Students clinical experiences meeting accreditation standards. - Appoint “Facility Coordinator” to oversee clinical experience and enable Student activities based on the agreed objectives. - Orient Students to the Program and applicable Exos rules and policies. - Maintain qualifications/ licenses required to provide clinical experiences to Students. - Promptly notify Institution of any student injuries, and arrange medical care per its policies, but without financial responsibility. | - Meet periodically to review key Program objectives. - Cooperate to supervise and evaluate Students, including providing feedback on Student’s performance throughout the Program.

Thereafter, it will automatically renew for successive one-year periods, unless either party provides at least 60 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal, to be effective as of the end of the then-current term; provided, however, that non-renewal shall not disrupt the clinical experience of any Student actively serving in the Program, and the Agreement shall remain effective as to such Student(s) until the end of their clinical experience. Following non-renewal by either party, no new Students will be placed at any Facility.

our_standard.text: 1.9.2. For Cause. This Agreement may be terminated for cause as follows:

preferred_variations.if:
B. For Cause. In the event the Institution or Exos fails in any substantial manner to perform as required herein, this Agreement may be terminated as described below:
Either  party  may  terminate  th
preferred_variations.to:
B. For Cause. In the event the Institution or Exos fails in any substantial manner to perform as required herein, this Agreement may be terminated as described below:
Either  party  may  terminate  this  Agreement  at  any  time,  upon  material  breach  of  any  of  its provisions by the other party; provided, however, that not less than thirty (30) days prior to termination, written notice shall be given by the non-breaching party to the breaching party that states the intention of the non-breaching party to terminate this Agreement, the nature of the material  breach  giving  rise  to  termination  and  shall  permit  the  breaching  party  reasonable opportunity to cure such material breach during said thirty (30) day period (" Cure Period ").
If the material breach is not resolved to the satisfaction of the non-breaching party during the Cure Period as provided in Section 6.2 (B)(1) above, the non-breaching party may immediately terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the breaching party.
In the event that termination of the Agreement by Exos pursuant to this Section 6.2 (B) disrupts the clinical experience of any Student(s) in the Program, the parties shall attempt, in good faith and using their best efforts, to continue Students' clinical experiences, and this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until such time as this Agreement may expire without disruption of said Students' clinical experience. During any time period in which notice of termination has been given and existing Students are completing the Program, no new Student may be placed at any Exos facility.
